claudeMd.what: Three decisions from this pass that a later editor would otherwise undo.
claudeMd.instruction: Append the paragraphs below to the end of the file's opening section, after the paragraph beginning 'The paragraph is two sentences and names no file or command'. Do not touch `## The house rules` other than as the second paragraph describes.
claudeMd.code:
`SetYourAssistant` sits directly under that paragraph, and it is the page's only task. The setting is
what decides which commands and which filenames step 1 shows a student, and until this card arrived
the page told them about it and never asked for it. **One move, and no `assistant.description`**: the
mode switch and the deck stay with the panel on the reasoning above, and the paragraph over the card
already says where the work happens. It is the only thing on the page a student is sent away to do.

`welcome.lead.2` is the course's **only** statement of what has to be installed, and the `{ready}` row
of `workshop`'s board is the only thing that checks it. Do not repeat either in `backend`. It names a
JDK 25 because all four `pom.xml` files pin `<java.version>25</java.version>`, so a Boot or toolchain
bump visits this paragraph in both languages.

Two sentences elsewhere on the page are load bearing for units that are not this one.
`how-workshops-work.1` **counts the workshops in its last sentence rather than claiming most steps have
one**, because they do not: step 1 closes on `recap` and step 3 on `impostor`. Measured off the
registries, so a step that gains or loses a board visits it. And rule three now ends `unless the step
says otherwise`, which exists for exactly one caller, `step1/workshop.one-window.1`, where the whole
hunt is deliberately worked in a single window. That clause is the only change the rule takes: the
justifying line cut from it stays cut.
